{"id":"persona-5s4b.1","title":"FetchJWTSVID enumerates all attestors serially on every request","description":"persona-grpc/src/service.rs:121-137 — fetch_jwtsvid() loops `for attestor in &self.attestors` and awaits `attestor.enumerate()` one at a time, on every single RPC, with no caching.

Each enumerate() is real I/O, not a cheap lookup:
- tailscale.rs:39-59 connects to a Unix socket, does an HTTP/1.1 round trip, read_to_end
- ssh.rs:86-94 connects to SSH_AUTH_SOCK and does a request/response round trip
- gpg.rs:105-115 spawns a `gpg` subprocess (process spawn + keyring read; tens of ms)
- oidc.rs:163 reads and JSON-parses up to 3 token cache files from disk

What goes wrong: per-request latency is the SUM of every probed source, and the GPG subprocess spawn alone dominates. On a machine with tailscale + ssh-agent + gpg active this is easily 50-150ms of serial work per FetchJWTSVID, paid by every consumer on every fetch. persona/src/main.rs:433 `watch` polls this every 30s and persona-nmh forwards browser requests through it.

Fix (no new dependency — tokio is already a workspace dep with features=["full"]): run the probes concurrently with tokio::task::JoinSet, collecting Ok(claims) and logging Err per attestor exactly as now. The loop body is unchanged; only the await is fanned out.

Note the result is only used to pick the single highest-assurance claim (service.rs:125-130), so ordering does not matter and concurrency is safe.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:56:22.829131756Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T20:56:22.829131756Z","labels":["efficiency","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.1","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:56:22.85108218Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

Each enumerate() is real I/O, not a cheap lookup:
- tailscale.rs:39-59 connects to a Unix socket, does an HTTP/1.1 round trip, read_to_end
- ssh.rs:86-94 connects to SSH_AUTH_SOCK and does a request/response round trip
- gpg.rs:105-115 spawns a `gpg` subprocess (process spawn + keyring read; tens of ms)
- oidc.rs:163 reads and JSON-parses up to 3 token cache files from disk

What goes wrong: per-request latency is the SUM of every probed source, and the GPG subprocess spawn alone dominates. On a machine with tailscale + ssh-agent + gpg active this is easily 50-150ms of serial work per FetchJWTSVID, paid by every consumer on every fetch. hire/src/main.rs:433 `watch` polls this every 30s and hire-nmh forwards browser requests through it.
